name: Dang Vu
line: Matt · fullstack engineer · TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node · Hanoi
paragraphs: I started in 2022 as a developer trainee at FPT Software, learning how software gets built by teams rather than by one person in a side project. That autumn I joined Bravebits to work on PageFly, a page builder that merchants use to build their storefronts.

I spent three years there. Early on I shipped whatever was assigned. What changed me was performance work: to make pages faster I had to stop guessing and start measuring, learn what the browser actually does with the code I write, and defend the tradeoffs to people who cared about the outcome and not the technique. That taught me to look for the constraint before writing anything. Later I worked on tooling that turned designs into editable pages, where the interesting part was not the model but deciding what to do when it got things slightly wrong.

Since November 2025 I have been at sending.ac, a much smaller team. The work is wider here: billing, authentication, integrations. Owning a feature from schema to UI, and being the person who gets called when it breaks, has made me a lot more careful about what I ship and a lot less precious about my own code.

Outside work I contribute upstream to tensorzero and nextest, mostly because reading someone else's codebase well is a skill I want to keep sharp. I spent a year writing Rust and compiling it to the browser, including an earlier version of this site. I still like Rust. I stopped shipping it to browsers.
